evidence.positive: Against the running app on localhost:50666, tenant mayo-mayo, driving GET /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/{caseId}/antibiotic-candidates (which drops the cached resolution and re-walks) plus POST /api/cds/medication-selection/{pmrn}/{caseId} as loopuser. (1) p-duodenal-ulcer, configured pathway 0 'CEFAZOLIN -> VANCOMYCIN' and pathway 1 'CEFAZOLIN AND METRONIDAZOLE -> (CIPROFLOXACIN AND METRONIDAZOLE) OR (CIPROFLOXACIN AND CLINDAMYCIN)', patient with no allergy: outcome RECOMMENDED, recommended [[CEFAZOLIN],[CEFAZOLIN,METRONIDAZOLE]], contraindicated [], and every step 2 option reported NOT_SELECTED - each pathway contributed its own first surviving step and stopped there. (2) Same procedure, patient with ANAPHYLAXIS to allergen a-cefazolin: outcome RECOMMENDED, recommended [[VANCOMYCIN],[CIPROFLOXACIN,METRONIDAZOLE],[CIPROFLOXACIN,CLINDAMYCIN]], contraindicated [CEFAZOLIN] only - the AND option 'CEFAZOLIN AND METRONIDAZOLE' died whole (step 1 CONTRAINDICATED) while METRONIDAZOLE was never named unsafe, both step 2 alternatives of pathway 1 survived, and pathway 0 kept its own VANCOMYCIN fallback. (3) p-oophorectomy-laparoscopic, configured pathway 0 'None' and pathway 1 'CEFAZOLIN -> CIPROFLOXACIN', no allergy: outcome OPTIONAL_PROPHYLAXIS recommending [[CEFAZOLIN]] - a procedure offering both drugs and no antibiotic. (4) Same procedure, patient with ANAPHYLAXIS to m-ciprofloxacin only: still OPTIONAL_PROPHYLAXIS recommending [[CEFAZOLIN]] with contraindicated [] - the drug the patient is anaphylactic to sits at a step the walk never reached, so it is neither offered nor named unsafe. (5) Same procedure with a-cefazolin allergy only: OPTIONAL_PROPHYLAXIS recommending [[CIPROFLOXACIN]], contraindicated [CEFAZOLIN]. (6) Alerts name survivors: selecting m-gentamicin on the cefazolin-allergic duodenal-ulcer case fired a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic with description 'For Duodenal ulcers, recommend: Vancomycin or CIPROfloxacin and MetroNIDAZOLE or CIPROfloxacin and Clindamycin' - the three survivors, not the configured cefazolin regimens.
evidence.negative: (1) Rule 5, every pathway must survive. Added ANAPHYLAXIS to m-vancomycin-iv on the cefazolin-allergic p-duodenal-ulcer case, so pathway 0 lost both of its steps. Outcome flipped RECOMMENDED -> ALL_CONTRAINDICATED, recommended [], contraindicated [CEFAZOLIN,VANCOMYCIN], and pathway 1's two surviving step 2 options were reported NOT_SELECTED rather than offered. Application log: 'Procedure p-duodenal-ulcer recommends nothing: 1 of its 2 pathways survived no option'. The withholding reaches the room, not just the debugger: selecting m-gentamicin on that case produced no alert at all, logged 'Rule evaluated: a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic -> false No antibiotic candidates for procedure type'. (2) A None pathway does not rescue a dead procedure. On p-oophorectomy-laparoscopic, added ANAPHYLAXIS to m-ciprofloxacin on top of the a-cefazolin allergy so both steps of the only drug pathway died. Outcome ALL_CONTRAINDICATED with recommended [], NOT NO_PROPHYLAXIS_INDICATED, even though the response shows pathway 0 as appliesToCase=true, noProphylaxis=true.
evidence.red_check: Two independent red checks, both reverted and both confirmed. (A) Pre-fix-style class swap. Copied ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService.java into the container, replaced @Slf4j with an explicit slf4j logger (lombok is not on the runtime classpath), and compiled two variants against /app/classes and /app/libs: the shipped logic, and one with rule 5 neutered by changing 'if (died > 0)' to 'if (false && died > 0)' in survivorsOf. Backed up the five shipped class files (main plus $1, $CaseSurvivors, $ProcedurePathways, $Walk) with md5sums, copied the neutered build into /app/classes/com/guided/orci/service, restarted the container. The identical duodenal-ulcer case then returned RECOMMENDED with recommended [[CIPROFLOXACIN,METRONIDAZOLE],[CIPROFLOXACIN,CLINDAMYCIN]] instead of ALL_CONTRAINDICATED, and the selection alert read 'For Duodenal ulcers, recommend: CIPROfloxacin and MetroNIDAZOLE or CIPROfloxacin and Clindamycin' - the sibling pathway's regimen actively recommended to the room for a patient whose bare-cefazolin route has no answer. That is exactly the behaviour rule 5 exists to prevent, so the absence assertion went red. Restored the backed-up class files, restarted, md5sums matched the pre-swap backup byte for byte (c305117c8e0c6336f2041a92c9bf84fd for the main class), and the case returned ALL_CONTRAINDICATED with recommended []. (B) Data flip on the None-does-not-rescue assertion. Set risk='HIGH' on p-oophorectomy-laparoscopic's drug pathway row in mayo-mayo.antibiotic_pathways so only the None pathway applied to the low-risk case. The ALL_CONTRAINDICATED case flipped to NO_PROPHYLAXIS_INDICATED with appliesToCase=false on the drug pathway, and the log emitted 'Operation ... has no antibiotic pathways to walk under tenant TenantKey[value=mayo-mayo]: [p-oophorectomy-laparoscopic drug=0 none=true]' - the outcome the negative asserts must not occur. Reverted risk to null and ALL_CONTRAINDICATED returned. The same flip applied to p-duodenal-ulcer's dead pathway 0 made pathway 1's withheld survivors reappear as RECOMMENDED, then was reverted. No pathway row in either procedure carries a non-null risk now, and all five scenarios were re-run green on the restored build.

caveats: Validated in the mayo-mayo tenant only; the shipped demo and mgb configurations contain no procedure with two pathways or with None beside drug pathways, so rule 4, rule 5 and OPTIONAL_PROPHYLAXIS are not reachable there as configured.

The rule-5 class swap flipped the guard rather than restoring pre-fix code: no commit in the repo references OR-2801, and the pre-walk model was a different schema, so there is no pre-fix version of the class to compile.

Contraindication was driven only by documented drug allergies (MedicationAllergyRule plus the cephalosporin cross-reactivity rules); the other FILTERS_ANTIBIOTIC_CANDIDATES rules were not used to rule a category out.

Cases were built through the admin create endpoints and never launched, so procedure risk was unrated and read as the LOW default; risk and acuity scoping were touched only as the lever for one data flip, not validated in their own right.
Multi-procedure coverage, SUPPRESSED_DISAGREEMENT and combination pathways were not exercised - they sit outside this ticket's single-procedure scope.
Medication toleration and per-reader allergy suppression, which the walk reads and which make the answer vary by user, were not exercised.

automation.assessment: Service-level coverage is already thorough and does not need duplicating: AntibioticPathwayResolutionSpecTest holds 73 tests, including or2792_duodenalUlcerFirstRouteHasNoFallbackAndSilencesTheProcedure (the rule-5 case validated here), noneDoesNotRescueAFullyInvalidPathway, laterStepsAreNotEvaluatedOnceAStepSurvives, andGroupLosesOneDrug_fallsToTheNextStep, orOptionSurvives_stopsAtTheFirstStep, separatePathwaysEachContributeTheirOwnStep and the debugger's appliesToCase and option-status reporting. The gaps are at the edges the walk is consumed through, and in the shipped configuration itself.
proposed_tests: Controller test on GET /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/{caseId}/antibiotic-candidates asserting it invalidates the cached resolution before walking and returns the outcome, pathway appliesToCase flags and option statuses - only the service method is covered today.

A guard over the shipped mayo, demo and mgb antibiotic-pathways.csv files that fails when a procedure has a pathway with no allergy fallback beside a sibling pathway that does, since rule 5 makes that shape silence the procedure and the affected list currently lives only as prose in ANTIBIOTIC_RESOLUTION_TEST_CASES.md.

Rule test that a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic abstains when ALL_CONTRAINDICATED was reached through rule 5 (one dead pathway beside a surviving sibling), distinct from the case where nothing survived anywhere.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: Walking a two-pathway procedure gave each pathway its own first surviving step, dropped an AND option whole when one of its drugs was unsafe, stopped at the first surviving step without judging the ones below it, and returned OPTIONAL_PROPHYLAXIS for a procedure offering both drugs and no antibiotic.

Negative: A pathway that lost every step made the whole procedure recommend nothing and its sibling's survivors were withheld from the alert, and a None pathway beside two dead drug steps still gave ALL_CONTRAINDICATED rather than no-prophylaxis-indicated.

Red check: Recompiling the walk in the container with the every-pathway-must-survive guard disabled made the case recommend the sibling pathway's regimen instead, and scoping the drug pathway out of the case turned the contraindicated verdict into no-prophylaxis-indicated; both were reverted and the shipped classes verified by checksum.

Automation: Service-level coverage already exists for every behaviour checked here, so the proposals are a controller test for the debugger endpoint and a guard over the shipped pathway files for the fallback gaps rule 5 makes fatal.
